texts: Secondary chordae may need to be sacrificed during closure of the VSD in an AVSD repair: B.
The ventricular patch is sewn to the right side of the septal crest, and small secondary chords that cross its path can be divided, while the primary chords supporting the leaflet edges are kept.
The common valve is divided into right and left components first; the VSD is closed, the leaflets are attached to the patch, and the atrial defect is closed last.
An annuloplasty can help a persisting central leak, and with a left SVC the coronary sinus is left draining to the right side.
In the picture, Franky cuts only a few thin secondary strings in the way of his patch, while the main strings stay.
Memory hook: cut the thin side strings, keep the main ones.
